evidence_items.publisher: Anthropic, PBC / U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
evidence_items.locator: Risk Factors, page 64; net-loss discussion and MD&A reconciliations
evidence_items.explanation: The filing reports net losses of $41.965 billion for 2025 and $80.748 billion for the first half of 2026, consistent with the company-loss portion of the claim. It also reports $974 million of operating profit in the June quarter and substantial noncash financing revaluations, so the net losses must not be described as equivalent cash losses or proof that every quarter's operations lost money.

evidence_items.locator: Section “Gotta spend money to make money”, first paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: Reporting on audited statements indicates substantial company-wide losses in 2025; the article also reports that removing a large restructuring charge still leaves a loss. This is reputable secondary reporting, not a directly obtained OpenAI filing.

evidence_items.locator: Section “Why the net loss is much larger”
evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic's positive first-half adjusted net income qualifies a blanket description of its economics; the amount and adjustments were checked against its S-1. It is a different accounting measure from reported net loss and does not by itself overturn a claim about a predominantly loss-making recent history.
